name: Magicka Templar Flexible PvE
author: DeadxxSmile / ATTB

progression_scope.description: Bundled ATTB progression build designed to guide a new character from leveling through the final target.

summary: Lightning-and-Ice holy battlemage with self-healing Sweeps, strong execute pressure, group resource synergy, and optional off-healing.

defaults.endgame_armor: 4 Light / 3 Medium overland; 6 Light / 1 Medium instanced

concepts.title: Primary resource
concepts.text: Put every normal attribute point into Magicka. Power of the Light costs Stamina but hybrid scaling does not justify splitting attributes.

concepts.title: Holy battlemage
concepts.text: Puncturing Sweeps makes this a close-to-mid-range magical fighter rather than a distant staff turret.

concepts.title: Execute
concepts.text: Below roughly 28% target Health, shift heavily into Radiant Glory while maintaining important long effects.

concepts.title: Duo value
concepts.text: Luminous Shards restores resources through its synergy; Extended Ritual or Breath of Life can replace damage when the duo needs safety.

craft.final_slots_note: Craft does not affect combat. Steed’s Blessing is the only universal default slot in the bundled builds; the other three Craft bar slots are intentionally left to personal activity. Rationer, Liquid Efficiency, Treasure Hunter, Gilded Fingers, and many other Update 50 utility stars are passive and should not be placed on the Champion Bar.
notes: Generic bundled-build priority: Steed’s Blessing first for universal movement quality of life, then broad passive economy/consumable value.
Required connector milestones for Rationer, Liquid Efficiency, and Treasure Hunter are inserted automatically from the canonical Champion Point catalog.
Do not copy character-specific Craft priorities blindly; a dedicated crafter, fisher, thief, or gold-farming character should use the optional branches that match the activity.

tips: Keep one Aedric Spear, Dawn’s Wrath, and Restoring Light skill on the active bar whenever XP lands.
Do not buy Tri Focus while using an Ice Staff; it changes blocking to consume Magicka.
Join Mages Guild early and collect lorebooks toward Meteor / Shooting Star.
Luminous Shards is valuable in a duo because the partner can activate the synergy for resources.
Ring of the Pale Order prevents other players from healing its wearer. Coordinate who equips it.
ESO Plus benefits belong to the subscribed account only. Crafted gear can still be traded to a player without access.
Recommended Class Mastery: Judgment’s Brand + Bright Harbinger after all three native class lines reach rank 50; subclassing disables them.
Master Ritualist is intentionally omitted: it does not materially help this solo/duo damage baseline, so keep those skill points for higher-value combat or crafting passives.
Medicinal Use is the only crafting passive treated as part of the combat baseline; other crafting trees are left to your character’s profession goals.
ATTB only treats Medicinal Use as a combat-required crafting passive. Spend the rest of your crafting skill points according to the professions you actually want to develop.

Champion Points in ATTB 3.1.1 are unlock-aware: follow the next-spend route instead of maxing connector stars before moving onward; come back for later targets after the first-pass route is established.
Update 50 base-bar refresh: use Soul Burst - Bleed / Lingering Torment / Resolve for the normal solo setup; Solar Barrage remains a full-damage or no-Scribing alternative.

class.summary: This build keeps all three native Templar skill lines for pure-class progression and Class Mastery access.

race.summary: Race changes damage, sustain, and utility slightly, but ordinary PvE content does not require the recommended option.
notes: Record the race you actually chose; ATTB keeps it separate from the build recommendation.

alliance.summary: Alliance primarily determines PvP faction and some story context. It does not change this PvE combat setup.
notes: Any Race, Any Alliance and Alliance Change Tokens can make race and alliance independent.

mundus.summary: The Thief increases Critical Chance and is the default damage Mundus for this launch build.
notes: Activate a different Mundus stone at any time to replace the current blessing.

front_weapon.summary: The front bar holds the main spammable, class burst, and offensive passives.

back_weapon.summary: The second weapon bar unlocks at character level 15 and normally carries longer-duration effects and support skills.

leveling_armor.summary: Mixed armor weights level multiple armor skill lines while Training traits accelerate experience gain.

endgame_armor.summary: The final weight mix balances damage passives, penetration, sustain, and Undaunted Mettle.

leveling_trait.summary: Training increases experience gained from kills. Replace leveling pieces freely rather than upgrading them heavily.

gear_cap.summary: Equipment stops scaling at Level 50 / CP160, so that is the first point where farming and upgrading permanent sets makes sense.

format_notes: Schema 4: flexible PvE progression, explicit hotbars and ultimates, complete loadouts, structured rotations, individual equipment slots, and acquisition-aware set groups.
Schema 4 supports metadata, class-line configurations, Scribing recipes, multiple loadouts, variants, quickslots, transformations, companions, performance notes, and namespaced extensions.

2026-08-20 bundled-build audit: Champion Point plans were rebuilt for ATTB 3.1.1 catalog-backed, unlock-aware routing; every default slottable now lives on the automatic route, optional branches remain opt-in, and Craft reflects current Update 50 passive/slottable classifications.

notes: Class Mastery requires all three native class skill lines at rank 50 and is unavailable while foreign class lines are active.
